name: Mount Rainier
summary: The highest mountain in Washington. Hazard Stevens and P. B. Van Trump received a hero's welcome in Olympia after climbing it in 1870; Fay Fuller made the first ascent by a woman in 1890.

routes.name: Disappointment Cleaver
routes.summary: The normal route to the summit, by way of Camp Muir. About 90 percent of attempts use the routes from Camp Muir.

routes.name: Emmons Glacier
routes.summary: By Camp Schurman on the northeast side, an alternative to Disappointment Cleaver with a lower technical challenge.

routes.name: Liberty Ridge
routes.summary: The ridge on the north side below Liberty Cap, considerably harder and more dangerous than the normal route.

landmarks.name: Paradise Inn
landmarks.summary: Built in 1916 and opened July 1, 1917. Many climbers start here.

landmarks.name: Camp Muir
landmarks.summary: The mountain's most-used high camp, named for John Muir. The Mountaineers built its guide shelter in 1916; the public shelter followed in 1921.

landmarks.name: Camp Schurman
landmarks.summary: The high camp on the Emmons Glacier route.

landmarks.name: Little Tahoma
landmarks.summary: A satellite peak, the remnant of a once larger Rainier. First recorded ascent August 29, 1894, by J. B. Flett and Henry H. Garrison.

name: Mount St. Helens
summary: Shown as it is today. On May 18, 1980, the north face collapsed and the summit dropped from 9,677 to 8,363 feet, so the Wy'easters knew a taller, whole mountain.

routes.name: Monitor Ridge
routes.summary: The standard route in the warmer months: about 4,600 feet of climbing in about five miles from Climbers Bivouac to the crater rim.

landmarks.name: Lava Dome
landmarks.summary: The dome inside the mile-wide, horseshoe-shaped crater left by the 1980 eruption.

landmarks.name: Spirit Lake
landmarks.summary: Before 1980 the lake had several lodges. One was run by Harry Truman, who had lived near the mountain since 1929 and refused to leave before the eruption.

name: Mount Adams
summary: The second-highest mountain in Washington. Andrew Glenn Aiken, Edward Jay Allen and Andrew J. Burge made the first ascent in 1854.

routes.name: South Climb
routes.summary: The easiest route to the summit, non-technical, up the south spur.

routes.name: North Cleaver
routes.summary: The ridge running almost due north from below the summit ice cap. The 1854 first ascent likely went this way.

landmarks.name: Pikers Peak
landmarks.summary: The false summit on the south side, 11,657 feet.

landmarks.name: Summit lookout
landmarks.summary: The Forest Service built a fire lookout on the summit, staffing it through 1924. Smoke and low cloud too often hid the view, and it was abandoned; miners later sheltered in it.

name: Mount Jefferson
summary: Oregon's second-highest mountain, also known as Seekseekqua. The first ascent was probably made by E. C. Cross and R. L. Farmer on August 12, 1888.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.summary: The line of the probable first ascent in 1888. The summit pinnacle is especially challenging.

landmarks.name: Jefferson Park
landmarks.summary: The lake basin on the mountain's northern slope, reached by the Whitewater and Pacific Crest trails.

landmarks.name: Whitewater Glacier
landmarks.summary: One of four named glaciers. It has shrunk considerably in recent years.

landmarks.name: Pamelia Lake
landmarks.summary: A popular lake on the southwest side with a limited number of visitors each day.

name: Three Sisters
summary: The third-, fourth- and fifth-highest peaks in Oregon. The height shown is South Sister's.

routes.name: South Sister Climber Trail
routes.summary: South Sister is the easiest of the three, with a trail all the way to the summit.

routes.name: Hayden climbers' trail
routes.summary: A climbers' trail on the east side, toward the Hayden Glacier between North and Middle Sister.

landmarks.name: North Sister
landmarks.summary: The most dangerous climb of the three because of erosion and rockfall, often called the "Beast of the Cascades." 10,090 feet.

landmarks.name: South Sister
landmarks.summary: The highest of the three, 10,358 feet.

landmarks.name: Collier Glacier
landmarks.summary: Between North and Middle Sister. It retreated 4,900 feet and lost 64 percent of its area between 1910 and 1994.

landmarks.name: Green Lakes
landmarks.summary: Lakes in the basin east of South Sister.
